answers.children: Yes — Old English Sheepdogs are good with children because their loyal and gentle nature makes them patient around kids while their size and herding instinct lead them to nudge and guide rather than nip. The thick long double coat and sturdy build let them absorb enthusiastic play yet their intelligence and affection keep interactions warm. Their protective side further suits family life with toddlers. (PawLabs child-friendly score: 8/10)
answers.other-pets: Yes — Old English Sheepdogs generally get along with other pets thanks to their affectionate and sociable temperament although their strong herding drive can prompt them to bump and round up cats or smaller dogs. Their intelligence helps them learn boundaries with early training while the protective instinct rarely turns aggressive toward household animals. The large powerful build means supervision prevents accidental knocks during play.
answers.exercise: Old English Sheepdogs need at least one to two hours of exercise daily or they grow bored and destructive because their herding background demands sustained activity. Long walks suit their rolling gait but they thrive when mental work such as fetch or agility is added to channel their intelligence and energy. The shaggy coat traps mud and debris so outdoor sessions require extra cleanup.
answers.shedding: Yes — Old English Sheepdogs shed heavily year-round with peaks in season because their thick long double coat constantly drops undercoat while the outer layer tangles easily. The dense shaggy texture traps loose hair indoors and mats form behind the ears or on the hindquarters unless brushed frequently. Their original farm role in harsh English weather produced this heavy coat that leaves noticeable fur on furniture and clothing.
answers.hypoallergenic: No breed is hypoallergenic and the Old English Sheepdog is not one of those commonly suggested for allergy sufferers because its long double coat sheds profusely and releases dander with every shake. The thick undercoat and shaggy outer layer hold onto allergens rather than minimise them so households with sensitivities should expect regular cleaning. Their protective and affectionate nature cannot offset the grooming demands either.
answers.training: Old English Sheepdogs are moderately easy to train because their high intelligence and eagerness to learn respond well to consistent guidance yet their stubborn streak surfaces if sessions lack structure. The breed’s herding background means they were developed to work independently with livestock so they may test boundaries rather than obey instantly. Early training prevents the protective instinct from becoming overly pushy around family or strangers.
answers.lifespan: Old English Sheepdogs live 10-12 years and their large heavy build combined with the demands of a thick long coat can influence robustness because the energetic herding frame requires steady weight management. Their intelligence and affectionate temperament encourage active lifestyles that support longevity while the original English farm selection for hardy weather resistance still shapes their overall constitution.
answers.size: Old English Sheepdogs reach 60-100 lb and stand 21-24 in at the shoulder so their substantial shaggy frame feels like a large teddy bear that can accidentally knock over furniture or people during enthusiastic greetings. The powerful build developed for nudging livestock across rugged English terrain gives them a rolling gait and impressive presence indoors. Their affectionate nature makes the size welcome for families seeking a protective companion.
answers.barking: Old English Sheepdogs bark moderately because their protective temperament produces a deep alert bark when strangers approach or something seems amiss yet they stay relatively quiet otherwise. Bred to herd livestock using size and body pressure rather than constant vocal commands the breed relies on presence more than noise. Their intelligence lets them learn when barking is unnecessary so excessive noise is uncommon in well-trained adults.
answers.apartment: No — Old English Sheepdogs do not suit apartment living because their high energy from herding work and large powerful build make settling indoors difficult without ample daily exercise. The thick long coat sheds heavily and requires space for grooming while their deep protective bark can disturb neighbours. Their affectionate and intelligent nature thrives better with room to move and engage in activities that prevent boredom.
answers.first-time: No — Old English Sheepdogs are not ideal as a first dog because their high grooming needs from the thick long coat and stubbornness if training is inconsistent demand experience and commitment. The energetic herding drive combined with their large size and protective instinct requires an owner who can provide structure and daily activity from the start so novices may feel overwhelmed by the scale of care involved.
